what: One motor turns the paper and a second carries an offset pen crank. Ink follows actual simulated poses. Sevenfold pattern: 2 paper turns and 7 pen turns trace a live curve on rotating paper. Two motors, a 20:60 mesh and an offset crank.
try: Reset to clear the paper, then run the selected pattern.
Watch the pen in the room frame and the trace in the paper frame.
Reset and compare the Fivefold, Sevenfold, Elevenfold and Eightfold examples.
why: The pen path must be expressed relative to rotating paper. Rational turn ratios allow both axes to return to their starting phase together. Independent servos create small transient phase errors.
matters: Changing reference frames explains apparent motion in rotating systems and robot tooling.
question: Will moving only the pen reproduce the same drawing?
answer: No. The rotating paper changes the coordinates in which the trace is recorded. Both measured motions are needed.
further: Compare the predicted closure with the last point of actual ink.
Virtual paper and ink do not model friction, slip or real marker pressure.
formula: paper coordinates = R(−paper angle) × (axis offset + R(pen angle) × crank vector)
